questions.prompt: What is the difference between ARG and ENV?

options.text: ARG is available at run time; ENV is only at build time
ARG is a build-time variable that is gone at run time; ENV is baked into the image and available while the container runs
Both are safe places to store secrets

questions.explanation: ARG exists only during the build and is not present in the running container. ENV is baked into the image and available to the process at run time.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended way to make one image behave differently in dev vs production?

options.text: Build a separate image per environment with the config hard-coded
Pass configuration through environment variables at run time
Edit the running container's files by hand
Use a different base image each time

questions.explanation: Environment variables (-e or --env-file) let the same image run everywhere, with only the configuration changing — a core twelve-factor idea.

questions.prompt: Which restart policy restarts a container after crashes and host reboots but respects a manual docker stop?
questions.explanation: unless-stopped behaves like always but does not restart the container if you deliberately stopped it.

questions.prompt: docker stop first sends the ______ signal to allow a graceful shutdown before forcing SIGKILL. (signal name)
questions.explanation: docker stop sends SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after a grace period (10 seconds by default) if the process has not exited.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true about configuration and exit codes? Select all that apply.

options.text: An exit code of 0 means the container exited successfully
Secrets should not be passed via ARG or ENV expecting them to be hidden
--env-file loads many environment variables from a file
By default, a container that stops is automatically restarted

questions.explanation: 0 means success, ARG/ENV are not safe for secrets, and --env-file loads variables in bulk. The default restart policy is 'no', so stopped containers stay stopped.

questions.prompt: Match each restart policy to its behavior.

pairs.right: Restart only on a non-zero exit code
Restart whenever it stops, including on reboot
Like always, but not after a manual stop

questions.explanation: The four policies range from never restarting to always restarting, with on-failure and unless-stopped covering the common middle-ground cases.
